title: Connection fallthrough and token-gap healing playbook for streaming outages
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-03-10 we observed a class of streaming client disconnects that led to truncated outputs and out-of-order token fragments for a subset of sessions. This ticket consolidates the incident findings into an actionable playbook: immediate mitigations (hotfixes), detection/alerting improvements, and medium-term protocol/runtime changes we will roll into runtime-1.22 and console-2026.03. The goal is to prevent token-gap exposure to clients, ensure safe automatic fallthrough to lower-throughput model variants, and provide reliable reassembly or replay semantics for resumed streams.
impact: High: affected ~0.8% of streaming sessions during the 45-minute capacity spike. Several production tenants reported partial responses and client-side retries. No data loss of user inputs was detected, but application-level errors increased and some customers escalated to support.
timeline: 2026-03-10 14:06 UTC - first SLO alerts for increased stream error rates
2026-03-10 14:09 UTC - Ops routed traffic away from overloaded region; partial reduction in new sessions
2026-03-10 14:12 UTC - telemetry shows abrupt connection closures with 100-200ms bursts of token fragments arriving after reconnect
2026-03-10 14:30 UTC - incident declared; mitigation: transiently reduce batching window in serving runtime
2026-03-10 15:00 UTC - traffic normalized; postmortem collection began
root_cause: Combination of overloaded session accept queues + overdue backlog of KV cache updates caused the serving runtime to emit incomplete token frames to the stream socket during prioritized cleanup. Clients reconnect and receive overlapping fragments that do not include a strict session checkpoint, resulting in token-gap and reassembly ambiguity. Additionally, our backpressure signals (internal token credits) were being dropped for a subset of fast-fail connections due to a race in the socket flush path introduced by recent batching changes.
short_term_fixes: Hotfix 1: Enforce atomic stream frame flush - PR #redwood/runtime@gh/PR-1378 deployed to prod (rollback-safe). This ensures partial frames are buffered server-side until fully formed.
Hotfix 2: Conservative accept throttling - temporary cap on new streaming sessions per host to reduce queue pressure (ops runbook updated).
Hotfix 3: Disable the new eager batch coalescing flag for canary traffic until additional telemetry is available.
Alerting change: New alert 'stream_token_fragment_rate' to trigger at 0.2% of sessions with fragmented tokens over 10m.
Client guidance: published support note for SDK teams describing retry behavior and how to request idempotent resume tokens from the server
long_term_actions: Action A: Implement explicit session checkpoints: assign monotonic stream sequence IDs at session start and ensure resume flow requires last-acked sequence. Target: runtime-1.22.
Action B: Backpressure signal hardening: add ACK-based credit reconciliation to prevent dropped credits during socket flush races.
Action C: Build server-side fragment reassembly and deterministic dedupe using sequence IDs so resumed sessions can request missing ranges for replay.

Action D: Router policy for graceful fallthrough: when capacity is constrained, automatically route streaming requests to compatible lower-cost model variants with preserved response shape and stream semantics.
Action E: Expand load-testing to include synthetic reconnects and partial-frame injection to validate resume semantics (extend chaos tests in perf-suite).
Action F: Update SDKs to surface resume tokens and provide 'resume_or_fetch_full' helper with exponential backoff and maximum reassembly window.
Action G: Add per-tenant SLA telemetry to detect tenants more sensitive to token-gap errors and trigger proactive capacity reservations in Dedicated
action_items: Marco Chen - Implement atomic frame buffer changes and add unit/integration tests (owner).
Leah Gomez - Lead design of session checkpoint protocol and draft spec on Confluence (owner).
SRE Team (oncall) - Add 'stream_token_fragment_rate' alert and dashboard tile; run emergency cap until protocol is hardened.
DX (SDK) - Expose resume token in public SDKs and add helper behavior; publish migration notes.
PM (Jonas Fischer) - Coordinate release window and customer communications; prepare support playbook and status page copy.
Security - Review sequence-id scheme for any fingerprinting risk (security_review_required=false).
notes: We intentionally avoid immediate schema changes to wire protocol until we validate with synthetic reconnection tests.
Client-side SDK changes should be backward compatible; servers will continue to accept existing resumptions but prefer sequence-id aware resumes when available.
Estimate of risk: medium during rollout of sequence IDs; mitigations include canarying and automatic fallback to legacy resume semantics.
